sanskrit_verse: धनस्त्रीहारिपुत्राणाम् ऋणभागो धनं हरेत् । पुत्रोऽसतोः स्त्रीधनिनोः स्त्रीहारी धनिपुत्रयोः ॥
transliteration: dhanastrīhāriputrāṇām ṛṇabhāgo dhanaṃ haret | putro'satoḥ strīdhaninoḥ strīhārī dhaniputrayoḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The portion of debt belonging to one who has been deprived of wealth, son, or wife shall be recovered by the heir; likewise, the son of a woman whose husband is deceased or absent inherits her property.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through continuity of duty and inheritance
Causation aligns with sequential manifestation of dharma-adharma
Capacity-based responsibility derives from relational integrity
Restoration logic ensures continuity of energetic and material balance
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual is dispossessed of wealth, son, or spouse AND there exists a designated heir THEN that heir assumes recovery rights proportionate to the loss.
IF a woman's husband is deceased or absent AND she possesses property THEN her son inherits said property automatically upon attaining legal capacity.
NO punitive action shall occur WHERE entitlement transfer follows pramāṇa-based lineage verification.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes threshold criteria for inheritance claims in absence of direct male lineage. The court must verify: (1) factual dispossession or absence, (2) presence of qualified heirs, and (3) alignment with sequential dharmic causality. Responsibility lies in ensuring rightful restoration without punitive intervention.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms cause-effect in inheritance based on relational status. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as lawful succession triggered by specific life conditions. Responsibility is proportional to relational capacity, not fault. There is no punishment—only reintegration of entitlement within conscious order.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Verification of dispossession event and identification of rightful heir
Responsibility assumption protocol: Legal recognition of heir’s duty to restore energetic-material balance
Capacity restoration: Ensuring heir possesses awareness and resources to execute lawful claim
Integrity reintegration: Public acknowledgment of restored lineage and entitlement
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority of Dharma. This law restores inheritance integrity through consciousness-aligned causality. Reality remains non-punitive. Dharma prevails through awareness, not force.
